registered_before: any LID-DS 2019 or LID-DS 2021 result under the tolerance rule below is computed
registered_after: the registered LID-DS 2019 run (C1 not met: 723/1,162, 34/7,706, p95 10.48 s) and these exploratory reads of it: (a) the library exploit-time convention gives 1,076/1,162; (b) of the 439 missed attack recordings, 353 have an alarm window ending before the registered exploit time and none after it (mean gap 0.36 s between that window end and the exploit time), 86 have no alarm (76 of them CVE-2014-0160); (c) every exploit_start_time of the release is a whole number of seconds (40 attack recordings checked per scenario, all integer)
what_stays: the registered result (C1 not met, 62.22 %) remains the primary result of lidds2019-confirmation-v2 and is reported first; no model, parameter or threshold changes

added_analysis.label_resolution_tolerance: the exploit times of LID-DS 2019 have a resolution of 1 s, so an attack recording also counts as detected when an alarm window ends after (exploit time - 1 s); latency is measured from (exploit time - 1 s), floored at 0; normal recordings unchanged
added_analysis.same_rule_on_lidds2021: the same 1 s tolerance applied to the LID-DS 2021 official split (exploit times with sub-second resolution) through the same code path, to show what the rule itself adds where labels are precise
added_analysis.status: post hoc: defined after the failure was seen; reported beside the registered result, never instead of it; C1 is evaluated on it only descriptively
